look_here_first: CEDAR ROSETTE GRASS: first find NARROW, thin spring blades (roughly 1.3–5.5 mm wide), then inspect a VERY SHORT fringe of ligule hairs (~0.25–0.5 mm). Ripe spikelets are about 3–3.5 mm and overlap D. oligosanthes. Source photo shows separate oval spikelets on threadlike stems, but neither measurable size nor tiny collar curtain. Leave provisional until same plant leaves and glumes are available.

Actual source-labelled macro shows several small narrow green spindle-shaped spikelets borne singly on delicate threadlike pedicels branching away from a slender axis. best_field_traits: Perennial rosette-grass; spring and late-season branched phases differ.
Vernal culms commonly have 4–7 thin stem leaves, often relatively narrow (approximately 1.3–5.5 mm broad in Central Texas treatment).
Upper leaf surface often finely hairy, underside much less hairy; margin and lower blade may carry a few long hairs with swollen bases.
True ligule often very short (~0.25–0.5 mm), requiring a macro view.
Open ovoid spring panicle; stalked/terminal obovoid spikelets roughly 3–3.5 mm.
Individual spikelets are awnless, with a lower sterile floret and fertile upper floret; precise glume characters need magnification.
crew_field_check: 1. Confirm original photo ROLE (flower macro, habitat view, or open panicle) before using a label; this image alone is NOT a verified same-plant key.
2. On living same-plant shoot find spring basal rosette and compare early spring versus late-season leafy secondary shoots.
3. Open the collar: photograph true hair-fringe ligule separately from hairs at the blade base, with mm scale.

4. Measure at least three mature ripe SPIKELETS with 1-mm ruler; size categories ~1.3–1.6 lindheimeri, 2.1–3.2 commutatum, ~2.9–4 oligosanthes, ~3–3.5 pedicellatum, but overlapping ranges prohibit pure size-only identification.
5. If rosette/collar/leaf base or mature spikelet dimensions unavailable, record Dichanthelium sp. and a source-determined tentative species.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Rooted spring culm with narrow 1.3–5.5 mm thin blade in profile against 1-mm scale
0.25–0.5 mm hair-fringe TRUE ligule seen at a separated blade/sheath junction
Mature green oval spikelet of about 3–3.5 mm and glumes with mm reference
Whole spring panicle AND autumn leafy secondary shoot from same verified plant

confused_with: other Dichanthelium species (not yet represented in this learner)
comparisons.key_distinctions: Versus D. oligosanthes, 3–3.5 mm spikelet size overlaps; focus on genuinely narrow thin culm blades and a ~0.25–0.5 mm true collar hair fringe against oligosanthes' often longer 1–4 mm fringe. Lindheimer has tiny 1.3–1.6 mm spikelets; commutatum has broader often cordate stem blades and minute/absent ligule. Hair fringe must be viewed at scale, not inferred from isolated panicles.
comparisons.photo_context: Four real already archived source-labelled images are incorporated into a genus comparison. The Lindheimer habitat photo does not display a measured spikelet; none proves collar/leaf base anatomy. Morphological ranges are literature-based, not measured from these photographs.
not_reliable_alone: Airy panicle silhouette in a single season
Habitat or presumed annual/perennial condition from clipped stem
Ligule hair lengths or spikelet sizes inferred from photos without rulers
The older D. acuminatum var. lindheimeri name interpreted as a new separate species
